traps.why: H₂O₂ oxidises sulfur (sulfoxide). An alkyl halide alkylates it: the sulfonium salt.
There is a reaction: CH₃I does change dimethyl sulfide.

explanation: The sulfur lone pair attacks the alkyl halide (SN2): a trialkylsulfonium ion with the halide as the counter-ion.

distractors.name: diethyl sulfide
distractors.why: With CH₃I, diethyl sulfide gives a different product (shown).

distractors.name: thiolane
distractors.why: With CH₃I, thiolane gives a different product (shown).
